title: Circuit buffer orchestrator and deterministic fallback choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a unified circuit-breaker layer that operates deterministically across dependency types (model endpoints, third-party services, and per-tenant quotas) and integrates with SLOs and multi-region failover. Current breakers are ad-hoc per-service and do not account for tenant priority or safe staged fallback behavior, which has led to inconsistent user experiences during regional spikes.
goals: Implement a Circuit Buffer Orchestrator (CBO) that computes trip decisions from multiple signals (latency quantiles, error rates, token consumption) and emits a composed policy per dependency/model/tenant.
Align trips to SLOs: decisions should be explainable in terms of SLO windows (p50/p95/p99 latency and availability) and tenant SLA weightings.

Provide deterministic, staged fallback choreography that preserves availability while bounding correctness regressions: fallback to cached prefixes, model-quantized variants, or read-only stubs in a controlled priority order.
Support multi-region soft-failover: traffic clamps, gradual reroute, and hysteresis to avoid global cascades.
Expose observability: detailed events and a dashboard with trip reasons, affected tenants, and rollback actions.
Automate safe rollouts and dry-run simulations to validate thresholds before enabling enforcement in production.
design_decisions: Use a two-layer decision model: local breaker evaluator (per node) for fast detection + central CBO for coordination and state reconciliation.
Trip rule = sustained signal deviation beyond dynamic threshold derived from rolling quantiles (baseline) + tenant multiplier + min-sample floor.
Hysteresis windows must be asymmetric: longer cool-down after enforced trip than detection window to avoid flapping.

Fallback choreography follows deterministic priority: 1) serve cached prefix/stale-with-indicators, 2) route to quantized-compatible model variant, 3) route to dedicated safety instance (lower capacity, high-availability), 4) return structured error with suggested retry/backoff and telemetry tag.
For multi-region failover, use incremental clamp percentages (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with per-step validation and circuit release on health recovery signals.

Support per-tenant SLO weightings: higher-tier tenants have higher trip thresholds and smaller probability of shedding; lower-tier tenants will be shed before higher-tier ones when capacity constrained.
trip_spec: Signals: p99 latency, error-rate (5xx), model-timeout counts, queue length, token-per-second consumption.
Baseline: rolling 24h median + 95th-percentile delta used to compute dynamic threshold; threshold_timeout_window = 5 min for detection.
Minimum sample: 200 requests in detection window OR fallback to static threshold to avoid noisy trips for low-traffic tenants.
Tenant multiplier: base_threshold * tenant_slo_multiplier (e.g., gold=1.5, standard=1.0, free=0.75).

Spike handling: rapid spike component uses interquartile range to identify transient bursts; require "sustained" flag (>=3 consecutive detection windows) to assert trip for transient-resistant workloads.
Graceful degrade rule: when trip asserted, compute allowed_routes in order of fallback choreography and apply proportionate shedding by tenant priority.
fallback_behaviors: Cached prefix serving: if prefix exists in KV cache and cache TTL > 30s, return cached response with header X-Redwood-Degraded: cached.
Quantized model variant: route to model-quantized variant with lower memory/latency and add X-Redwood-Degraded: quantized.
Safety instance: route to read-only small model instance optimized for availability (returns conservative outputs). Tag responses with X-Redwood-Degraded: safety.
Stale-with-indicator: serve stale cached completion with small inline disclaimer and telemetry event for evals, allowed only for non-sensitive workloads.
Reject with structured fallback: if no safe fallback available, return a structured error that includes suggested retry-after and a guarantee of queued retry where tenant has queued quota enabled.
Telemetry: every fallback path emits an event with reason, tenant_id, model, region, trip_threshold, and selected fallback path.
observability: Dashboard panels: trips over time by region/model/tenant, p99 latency pre/post trip, fallback counts and types, rollback actions, synthetic test pass rates.
Event store: retain detailed trip events for 90 days in infra logs and 365 days in compressed cold storage for incident investigations.
Alerting: SRE alerts on persistent trips for >30 minutes affecting >5% of traffic, and PM alerts for any trip that impacts a gold-tier tenant.
Request tagging: add deterministic trip-reason tags to traces so downstream evals and cost tools can correlate cost and quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: CBO prototype acts as a central adjudicator and returns deterministic trip decisions in dry-run mode for three sample dependencies (model-serving, redis-cache, external-rate-limiter).
Trip decisions include human-readable reason codes and the inputs that caused the trip (window metrics and tenant multiplier).
Fallback choreography executed in canary (10% traffic) for a non-sensitive test tenant with clear telemetry and no customer-visible data loss beyond annotated degradation.
Dashboard shows per-region trip counts, affected tenant list, and fallback distribution in the canary run.
Automatic rollback policy can be triggered manually via Console and will revert routing to primary model within 5 minutes if health signals return to baseline.
Unit and integration tests cover decision logic, fallback path selection, and multi-region clamp sequencing.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize thresholds and priority matrix; land RFC and design doc in Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RES/CBO-RFC).
Phase 1 (dry-run): implement local evaluator and central CBO in dry-run for model-serving paths; run for 2 weeks and gather telemetry.
Phase 2 (canary): enable enforcement for internal test tenants and 5 internal services at 10% of traffic for 72h. Observe and iterate.
Phase 3 (gradual expansion): expand to 25% -> 50% -> 100% for non-sensitive workloads; enable tiered tenant shedding globally after 2 weeks of stability.
Phase 4 (full launch): enable for all regions with SRE playbooks and an on-call rotation that includes the runtime and model-onboarding engineers.
testing_plan: Simulated spike tests using locust harness across regions with synthetic prompts (link: https://github.com/redwood/infra-load-tests/pulls/421).
Chaos injection: introduce delays/failures in model-serving clusters and validate CBO decisions and the absence of cascading global trips.
Regression suite: ensure no increased 4xx/5xx rates for gold-tier tenants post-fallback-choreography enablement.
SLO validation: automated check that p99 latency and availability SLOs for gold tenants remain within targets at 95% after fallback enabled.
notes: Trade-offs: dynamic thresholds reduce false trips for workloads with diurnal patterns but add complexity and state. We accept this complexity because false trips have higher customer impact than delayed trips.
Open question: should we centralize tenant multipliers or allow tenant teams to request overrides via Console? Proposal: central default + Console request workflow for exceptions.
Coordination: schedule an SRE tabletop to validate recovery playbooks and runbook links before canary (owner: Markus).
